meta.storyTitle: Per-review-type checkpointing and temp-folder lifecycle make a review resumable and its final result durable

summary.prose: This Story adds the generic review-checkpoint record and the .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder lifecycle that make a review resumable after a crash and its final result durable after cleanup. A checkpoint is written automatically after each completed unit of work -- a round for design review, a Task for code review -- and a resume reads it back to skip what already finished. Before the temp folder is ever deleted, the final round's output is copied into durable storage first.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Alternative a2 wins: one shared round-driver function in a new sibling module under src/workflow/ (outside review-history/, which is being retired from rather than extended) takes a small per-review-type hook set -- the grounding/findings call, checkpoint granularity, and finding taxonomy/severity -- and runs the identical round cycle, checkpoint lifecycle, and reconciliation call for every review type.

ownedContracts.name: Review checkpoint record
ownedContracts.purpose: The generic 'review checkpoint' JSON side-record and the .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder lifecycle (per-review-type granularity, durable copy before deletion, reviewId as one identity), per k1/k7/k8/lc4.

consumedContracts.name: Review-type hook set
consumedContracts.purpose: The small hook set (grounding/findings call, checkpoint granularity, taxonomy/severity) that is the only thing legitimately differing per review type, consumed by the round-driver, per the Epic's one-shared-process framing (Story s1 ac1/ac2).

boundary.internal: The exact per-review-type granularity mapping (round-level for design review, per-Task for code review) and the durable-copy-before-deletion mechanics stay internal to s5; no other Story's type depends on ReviewCheckpoint's internals beyond what sc1's round-driver needs to call it.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The round-driver function itself -- what it does internally to run the grounding+findings, reconciliation, render+present and checkpoint-write cycle -- stays private to s1; no other Story's type depends on the driver's internals, only on the hook contract sc1 exposes.

Which exact per-review-type severity scales exist beyond the HIGH/MED default, and how a review type's Feedback implementation declares its own, stay internal to s2; no other Story's type depends on Finding's shape.

How the reconciliation LLM call is actually prompted, and how it reads the temp folder's audit trail when needed, stay internal to s3; no other Story's type depends on ReconciliationResult's internals beyond its verdict shape.

The exact docgen docType registration and MD rendering logic (including the resolved/still-open/contradicted annotation rule scoped to this round's own corrections) stay internal to s4; no other Story's type depends on the renderer's internals.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase B — taxonomy, reconciliation, rendering, checkpointing

nonFunctional.performance: Checkpoint write/read (sc5) is a single small JSON file write/read per completed unit of work (a round, or a Task), adding no I/O beyond what the round cycle already performs.
nonFunctional.durability: The final round's review-output JSON is copied into durable artifact storage before the .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder is deleted at a terminal state (k7), so a completed review's result survives after the ephemeral working folder is gone.

api.name: writeCheckpoint

parameters.name: checkpoint
parameters.purpose: The reviewId and the unit (round or Task) that just finished -- written automatically by the round-driver's cycle, with no agent-driven step (ac1/k6).

returns.meaning: Resolves once the checkpoint JSON has been written to .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/checkpoint.json.

preconditions: Called only after a full unit of work (round, or Task) has actually completed -- never mid-cycle
postconditions: The written checkpoint.json reflects exactly this call's checkpoint argument, overwriting any prior checkpoint for the same reviewId

api.name: readCheckpoint

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.purpose: Identifies which review's checkpoint to read back on resume (ac2).

returns.meaning: The last-written checkpoint for this reviewId, or undefined when no checkpoint exists yet (a review that never completed its first unit).

postconditions: A resume that reads a defined checkpoint re-runs only the unit of work after lastCompletedUnit, never a unit already completed

api.name: finalizeReview
api.signature: function finalizeReview(reviewId: string, finalOutput: unknown): Promise<void>

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.purpose: Identifies which review has reached a terminal state (ac3).

parameters.name: finalOutput
parameters.purpose: The final round's review-output JSON to copy into durable artifact storage before the temp folder is deleted.

returns.meaning: Resolves once finalOutput has been durably persisted and the .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder has been deleted.

preconditions: Called only once a review has reached a terminal state -- never mid-review
postconditions: finalOutput is copied into durable artifact storage BEFORE the .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder is deleted -- this ordering is never reversed (ac3/k7)
After this call resolves, .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ (including its checkpoint.json) no longer exists

dataModel.details: interface ReviewCheckpoint { readonly reviewId: string; readonly lastCompletedUnit: { readonly kind: 'round' | 'task'; readonly ref: number | string }; } -- exactly sc5's HLD interfaceSketch, unchanged. A generic JSON side-record stored at .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/checkpoint.json, independent of ReviewContext's own fields (lc4) -- ReviewContext does not exist yet (confirmed in s1's decision-trace bundle), so this Story's reviewId identity guarantee (ac4) covers only its own half: checkpoint.reviewId equals the temp folder's name, by construction.

writeCheckpoint's granularity (round vs Task) is determined by whatever sc1's RoundDriverHooks.checkpointGranularity names for that review type; this Story's contract does not redefine or re-derive that mapping, only reads it.

errorCases.scenario: writeCheckpoint's file write to .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/checkpoint.json fails (e.g. disk error, permissions)
errorCases.detection: the underlying filesystem write call rejects
errorCases.response: writeCheckpoint propagates the rejection to the caller rather than resolving as if the checkpoint had been saved
errorCases.userImpact: the caller knows the checkpoint did not persist, instead of believing a resume-safety guarantee exists that was never actually written

errorCases.scenario: finalizeReview's copy of finalOutput into durable artifact storage fails
errorCases.response: finalizeReview propagates the rejection and does NOT proceed to delete the .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder -- the ordering in ac3/k7 is never reversed even on failure
errorCases.userImpact: a review's final result is never lost to a failed copy silently followed by deletion; the temp folder (and its data) stays intact as a fallback until the copy can be retried

errorCases.scenario: finalizeReview's deletion of the .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder fails after the durable copy has already succeeded
errorCases.detection: the folder-deletion operation rejects, observed strictly after the durable-copy step already resolved
errorCases.response: finalizeReview propagates the rejection, but by this point finalOutput is already safely durable -- only cleanup is incomplete, not the review's result
errorCases.userImpact: the review's final result is safe; a leftover temp folder is the user-visible residue of a failed cleanup, not data loss

edgeCases.input: readCheckpoint is called for a reviewId whose first unit of work has not completed yet (no checkpoint.json exists)
edgeCases.expected: readCheckpoint returns undefined, not an error -- a review that has not completed anything yet is a valid, expected state

edgeCases.input: writeCheckpoint is called twice in a row for the same reviewId (e.g. a retried call after a transient failure)
edgeCases.expected: the second call's checkpoint overwrites the first in checkpoint.json; no duplicate-write error or merge logic is needed

edgeCases.input: lastCompletedUnit.ref is a string (a code-review Task identifier) rather than a number (a design-review round)
edgeCases.expected: ReviewCheckpoint accepts either, exactly as sc5's own interfaceSketch types ref: number | string -- no special-casing per review kind inside this Story's contract

alternativesConsidered.name: Flat ReviewCheckpoint per sc5's sketch, plus three small side-record functions keyed by reviewId alone
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: interface ReviewCheckpoint { reviewId, lastCompletedUnit } exactly as sc5 sketches it; writeCheckpoint/readCheckpoint/finalizeReview operate on '.insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/checkpoint.json', with granularity (round vs Task) read from sc1's RoundDriverHooks.checkpointGranularity, never redefined here.
alternativesConsidered.approach: interface ReviewCheckpoint { readonly reviewId: string; readonly lastCompletedUnit: { readonly kind: 'round' | 'task'; readonly ref: number | string }; } -- exactly sc5's HLD interfaceSketch. Three functions: writeCheckpoint(checkpoint: ReviewCheckpoint): Promise<void> (called automatically by the round-driver after a full round/Task cycle completes, per ac1 -- no agent-driven step); readCheckpoint(reviewId: string): Promise<ReviewCheckpoint | undefined> (used on resume to skip already-completed units, per ac2); finalizeReview(reviewId: string, finalOutput: unknown): Promise<void> (copies the final round's review-output JSON into durable artifact storage, then deletes the .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder, per ac3). All three key purely off reviewId as a plain string -- the folder name and checkpoint.reviewId are the same value by construction, satisfying this Story's own half of ac4/k8; ReviewContext's header-level reviewId is a separate, not-yet-existing field this Story cannot verify.
pros: Matches sc5's HLD interfaceSketch exactly, field-for-field -- no invented structure.
Does not redefine checkpoint granularity (round vs Task) -- consumed from sc1's RoundDriverHooks exactly as the HLD frames it, avoiding scope overlap with s1.
Smallest shape that satisfies ac1 (automatic write), ac2 (resume skips completed units), and ac3 (durable copy before deletion) -- three small functions, each doing exactly one documented thing.
cons: This Story's contract alone cannot prove ac4's full claim (reviewId is the SAME identity as ReviewContext's header field) since ReviewContext doesn't exist yet -- only this Story's own half (checkpoint.reviewId === folder name) is provable here.

alternativesConsidered.name: Stateful ReviewSession class bundling checkpoint + folder lifecycle together
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A `ReviewSession` class wraps write/read/finalize into one object with internal mutable state, instead of three independent functions.
alternativesConsidered.approach: class ReviewSession { constructor(reviewId: string); writeCheckpoint(unit): Promise<void>; readCheckpoint(): Promise<ReviewCheckpoint | undefined>; finalize(finalOutput): Promise<void>; } -- the object tracks its own open/closed lifecycle state internally across calls.
pros: One object per review could centralize folder-path computation instead of each function recomputing it from reviewId.
cons: Introduces unrequested statefulness (an open/closed lifecycle state machine) that none of ac1-ac4 ask for -- each acceptance criterion describes one call at one point in the cycle, not a session object's lifetime.
Harder to unit test each operation in isolation (must construct + drive the object through prior calls to reach a given state), where a1's plain functions take exactly what one operation needs.
No consuming Story (sc1's round-driver is the only consumer, per the HLD context) asked for session-object semantics; it just needs to call three operations at the right points in its own cycle.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Functionally equivalent to a1 on every acceptance criterion, but introduces unrequested statefulness (an open/closed session lifecycle) with no acceptance criterion asking for it, at the same cost.

alternativesConsidered.name: Checkpoint stored as a field on ReviewContext itself, instead of a separate side-record
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Fold lastCompletedUnit directly into ReviewContext's own fields rather than keeping ReviewCheckpoint as an independent JSON side-record.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add a `checkpoint: { kind, ref }` field directly onto the (not-yet-existing) ReviewContext type, read/written as part of the context object itself rather than a separate file.
pros: One fewer file to read/write per round, if ReviewContext is already being persisted anyway.
cons: Directly contradicts lc4: 'A review's checkpoint is a generic review checkpoint JSON side-record, independent of ReviewContext's own fields' -- this is an explicit HLD invariant violation, not a refinement.

Requires ReviewContext to exist and be mutated in-place on every unit completion; ReviewContext doesn't exist yet (confirmed in s1's decision-trace bundle), and even once it does, it belongs to the companion Epic (50cde239426d6e2a), not this Story -- folding checkpoint state into it would mean redesigning another Epic's type, far outside this Story's or even this Epic's boundary.

Loses the clean, independent deletion story ac3 relies on: a side-record inside .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ can be deleted wholesale with the temp folder; a field folded into ReviewContext would need to be explicitly cleared instead, since ReviewContext itself is not deleted.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates sc5's own stated invariant (lc4) outright, breaks ac3's clean deletion ordering, and depends on redesigning a type owned by an entirely different Epic -- disqualifying regardless of cost.

openQuestions: ac4 requires reviewId to be the same identity as both the .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder's name AND a header-level field on ReviewContext. This Story's design fully satisfies its own half (checkpoint.reviewId === folder name, by construction) but cannot verify the ReviewContext-side half, since ReviewContext does not exist yet anywhere in the codebase -- confirmed by direct grep and by the companion shared-reviewcontext-data-model Epic's (50cde239426d6e2a) own HLD, which explicitly defers assembling it as Non-Goal follow-on work. This Epic's own DEF already documents this as a HIGH-risk item (line 70): the companion Epic must incorporate a header-level reviewId field before this Story's full ac4 guarantee can be implemented and verified end-to-end. Not a new gap -- surfacing it for the cross-review pass and for a future Story in the companion Epic to track explicitly.
